Connect another database package to a user's sign-in

Source: R/session.R
oauth_db_connect.Rd

Use a database package that accepts access tokens with a visitor's Shiny sign-in. This is the general helper for drivers without a dedicated shinyOAuthDB function. It supplies the user's token when opening the connection and keeps that connection in their Shiny session.

Usage

oauth_db_connect(
  authorization,
  connect = DBI::dbConnect,
  ...,
  token_arg = "token",
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  disconnect = NULL,
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

connect

Function that opens the connection, such as DBI::dbConnect.

...

Named arguments for connect, excluding the token argument.

token_arg

Name of the argument that receives the user's access token.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

disconnect

Function to close the connection. By default, DBI connections use DBI::dbDisconnect(); other objects have no cleanup.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression to get the database connection. Before sign-in, it waits quietly like shiny::req().

Details

Create the helper inside server() so each visitor has their own connection. Call con() before each operation; it checks the current authorization and reuses a valid connection. Sign-out, account changes, loss of required permissions and session end trigger cleanup.

A connection you save separately may keep copied credentials, depending on the driver. Obtain it through con() each time. A valid DBI connection can stay open through token renewal; a broken one reopens on the next call.

If token refresh is running, reactive outputs wait until it finishes. A button-triggered query may need another click. min_valid_for checks the token's remaining lifetime at the start; it doesn't guarantee validity throughout a long query.

For functions that accept a token on every request, use oauth_db_token() or the source's API client.

See also

oauth_db_token(). For saved results and connection lifetime, see vignette("getting-started", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Inside server(); client configured for Azure PostgreSQL:
con <- oauth_db_connect(
  auth$connection,
  connect = DBI::dbConnect,
  drv = RPostgres::Postgres(),
  token_arg = "password",
  target = "postgres",
  host = "example.postgres.database.azure.com",
  dbname = "reporting",
  user = "reporting-readers",
  sslmode = "verify-full"
)
} # }
